$comment: OMN-17957. The command vocabulary of a credential rotation, re-issue or
revoke, and the two people who may approve one.
Read by plugins/onex/hooks/lib/credential_rotation_guard.py, which is
invoked by the pre_tool_use_credential_rotation_guard.sh PreToolUse hook.
The vocabulary lives here, not in the checker, so adding a shape is a
config edit visible in one place rather than a rule a reader has to infer
from a Python literal.
JSON rather than YAML deliberately, matching agent_model_allowlist.json and
ticket_creation_policy.json in this directory: the checker sits on a
fail-closed enforcement path, so it parses its own policy with the standard
library alone. A missing PyYAML in the resolved interpreter would otherwise
turn into a refusal of Bash traffic on the machine.
There is deliberately NO escape entry -- no wildcard shape, no exempt
marker, no allow_all. An unapproved rotation is the defect this guard
refuses, and a sanctioned spelling for it is a sanctioned incident.
approvers -- EXACTLY TWO, and the checker refuses a policy that names a
different number. The operator ruling of 2026-09-05 is that every
credential rotation goes through explicit approval by the operator or by
Jake; no agent, lane or codex message is approval, so there is no third
name that can be added by config. Widening this list is a decision about
who may authorise a rotation, and it belongs in a reviewed change to the
checker's own guard rail, not in a config bump.
consent_ledger_paths / consent_ledger_path_prefixes -- the ONLY files a
ROTATION-CONSENT citation may name, resolved under $OMNI_HOME. The
rolling ledger is the append-only, mutex-protected, committed
coordination surface named by omni_home CLAUDE.md rules 18 and 19; the
archive prefix is where a ledger roll writes. A lane that could cite any
file it can write has not been gated at all, so a citation naming
anything else is refused and a path that escapes $OMNI_HOME is refused
before it is opened.
rotation_shapes -- each is matched against the TOKENS of one shell segment,
never against the raw text. Token matching is what keeps `echo 'aws
secretsmanager rotate-secret'` and a grep for the vocabulary out of the
gate: the program of those segments is echo and grep, so no shape
applies. Raw-substring matching would fire on prose that merely mentions
a verb -- omni_home CLAUDE.md rule 15, the OCC#7213 shape, a gate firing
on documentation about the gate.
programs      -- the segment's program, by basename. sudo/env/command and
leading VAR=value assignments are stripped first.
all_of        -- every regex must match at least one token.
any_of        -- at least one regex must match at least one token. This
is where the READ/WRITE split lives: a shape lists only
the MUTATING subcommands, so `get-secret-value`,
`describe-secret`, `list-secrets`, `get`, `describe` and
a bare `-o name` read are outside every shape and are
never gated. Reads are not allowlisted; they simply
match nothing.
adjacent      -- at least one pair of consecutive tokens must match. Used
for `-X DELETE` where the method is a separate token.
credential_flags     -- flags whose FOLLOWING token names the credential.
credential_patterns  -- token regexes whose group 1 names the credential.
credential_skips_flag_values -- when true, a token that IS a flag, or
that immediately follows a value-taking flag, is skipped
while reading the credential. kubectl needs it so that
`-n onex-dev` does not read the NAMESPACE as the
credential; psql must NOT set it, because there the
credential lives inside the `-c` flag's own value.
A shape that matches but whose credential cannot be read is REFUSED, not
allowed: the consent row is checked by scope, and a scope check against
an unknown credential proves nothing.
kubectl rollout restart is deliberately absent from every shape. It is
the consumer-restart half of the remedy the 2026-09-05 ruling requires --
the half the 2026-08-30 rotation omitted for the Infisical operator
Deployment, which is what froze secret sync cluster-wide for five days.
A gate that made the correct repair harder than the mistake would be
routed around.

rotation_shapes.description: DELETE /api/v3/secrets/raw/<KEY> -- removes a secret from an Infisical path. Used on 2026-08-30 to delete the org-admin pair from /dev/onex-runtime/.
PATCH/POST/PUT /api/v3/secrets/raw/<KEY> -- writes a new secret value into an Infisical path. The prepared write step of the 2026-08-27 rotation runbook.
infisical identity ... client-secret create -- mints a new Universal Auth client secret for a machine identity.
infisical identity ... client-secret revoke -- retires a Universal Auth client secret. The second half of the 2026-08-30 operator-k8s rotation.
kubectl create secret -- writes a credential-bearing Secret. Used to push the rotated Infisical pair into universal-auth-credentials.
kubectl delete secret -- destroys a credential-bearing Secret. Used on the orphaned auth/universal-auth-credentials copy.
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value / create-secret -- writes a new secret value.
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret / cancel-rotate-secret -- drives a rotation directly.
aws secretsmanager update-secret / delete-secret / restore-secret -- mutates an existing secret.
aws iam create-access-key -- issues a new long-lived IAM credential.
aws iam delete-access-key / update-access-key -- revokes or disables a live IAM credential.
gh secret set -- writes an Actions/Dependabot/Codespaces secret.
gh secret delete -- removes an Actions secret, breaking every workflow that reads it.
kcadm create|update clients/<id>/client-secret -- regenerates a Keycloak client secret.
psql ALTER ROLE|USER ... PASSWORD -- changes a database login credential.
